messages:
maria_support: Hey team, customer reporting tool.call failing when arg contains an XML blob inside a JSON string. payload accepted elsewhere but our parser returns 400
kevin_customer: repro steps: POST /v1/toolcall with body: {
  \"tool\": \"html-processor\",
  \"args\": \"<note><to>A</to><from>B</from></note>\"
} -> 400 invalid tool args
jon_engineer: @maria_support thanks. can you paste exact request (headers + body)? also which SDK/agent?
maria_support: pasted headers: Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, Authorization: Bearer <redacted>. Using fetch in node. here's minimal curl we asked customer to try:
```\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \\
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\
 -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
 -d '{\"tool\":\"html-processor\",\"args\":\"<note><to>A</to><from>B</from></note>\"}'\n```
kevin_customer: right, that curl is exactly what fails; if i escape the angle brackets as HTML entities it succeeds, but that's not desirable.
jon_engineer: Hmm. Do we unescape/validate args as JSON then pass to tool? Could be our JSON parser choking on raw <...> in strings because of a validator that treats it as harmful payload.
rachael_level2: I see two failures in logs around that ts: parse_error: invalid_tool_args and a sanitizer warning: 'suspicious_markup' flagged. ops_bot: Incident note inserted for 2115550192: potential false-positive sanitizer for tool args containing XML.
maria_support: customer insists their payload is valid JSON string — they already tried a JSON validator.
jon_engineer: Can we reproduce locally. trying quick test in node with the same payload...
jon_engineer: (2m later) reproduced minimal case using node-fetch: server returns 400 and body shows error: \"Tool args validation failed: contains disallowed markup\"
rachael_level2: That implies a validation rule blocking angle brackets inside args. Is that policy tied to WAF or an API-level sanitizer?
jon_engineer: Grep shows a validator in packages/tooling/src/validateArgs.ts with a rule: rejectIfMarkup with regex /<[^>]+>/ flagged as high risk. It was added last year to block inline scripts in rich text tool args.
kevin_customer: from product POV our tool expects HTML/XML snippets so this is a regression for us. Do you have a workaround?
maria_support: told customer to base64 encode the XML as temporary workaround. Not ideal.
jon_engineer: Proposed options: 1) relax validator to allow XML for trusted tools (tool allowlist), 2) whitelist per-customer, 3) special escaping in SDKs. I can prepare a patch to check tool name and skip rejectIfMarkup for html-processor and similar.
rachael_level2: We need an RFC + security review before removing validator. For immediate relief, can we add a header to signal raw args: X-Allow-Markup: true?
jon_engineer: quick fix: support team can enable a feature-flag in the customer's account to bypass markup check. I will add a targeted rollout flag.
maria_support: customer accepted toggle, asked for ETA.
jon_engineer: I'll push feature flag change to staging and test. ETA 2 hours. Steps I took: updated validateArgs to short-circuit when metadata.tool in ALLOW_MARKUP_TOOLS, ran unit tests, smoke tested curl — now returns 200 for the embedded XML case.
maria_support: any security notes?
jon_engineer: We added explicit allowlist and logged the bypass reasons. Security requested audit trail and sanitized copies in logs; they are okay with allowlist for Named tools. Will open PR and include test cases for nested tags, CDATA, and angle-escaped content.
kevin_customer: thanks, please let me know when flag is live for our org.
maria_support: created customer ticket and queued for flag rollout. tagging @ops_bot to schedule prod rollout window. ops_bot: Scheduled canary rollout at 2026-03-17T22:00Z for account kevin-corp with monitoring alerts.
jon_engineer: PR link: https://git.redwood.internal/pr/7421 (internal). patch note: \"validateArgs: allow markup for trusted tools; add audit log\"
rachael_level2: closing loop checklist: reproduce -> identify validator -> create allowlist patch -> security review -> feature flag -> customer toggle -> monitor. set status: awaiting prod canary.
maria_support: thanks team. will update customer when canary completes. :white_check_mark:
